lenses.lens: CROSS-MODULE SHARED CODE: exa vs brave helper duplication
lenses.summary: The two modules share large, near-identical plumbing copied verbatim or with only trivial renames. Verified by line-range diffs: (1) a ~200-line dual sync/async wrapper set (exa 133-334, brave 522-723) that is BYTE-IDENTICAL, including the module-tail `_apply_async_to(globals())` hook (exa:5988, brave:7213); (2) a ~80-line API-key lookup trio `_seek_api_key`/`_read_key_file`/`_get_api_key` (exa 411-488, brave 890-967) that is BYTE-IDENTICAL (only the `_API_KEY_NAMES`/`_API_LABEL` constants differ, which is the intended parameterization); (3) the HTTP-engine core `_http/_pool/_retry_after_seconds/_fanout` plus the module globals `_ENGINE_LIMITS/_CLIENT/_WORKERS` (exa 26-79, brave 23-80) that differ only by trivial renames (`follow_redirects=True/False`, `thread_name_prefix="exa"/"brave"`, docstrings). These three are strong candidates for lifting into an internal `_common` module; the only intended differences are the redirect flag, the worker-name prefix, and the key-name/label constants, all of which would need to be parameterized. By contrast, the domain/url helpers are DIVERGENT (exa `_domain_of` is a registrable-domain label-slicer; brave `_url_host` is a hostname+www-strip) and should NOT be merged. Also note `_request` is NOT near-identical (exa POST + x-api-key + ExaError taxonomy; brave GET + X-Subscription-Token + BraveError taxonomy + fallback endpoints) and shares only the engine primitives, so a `_common` lift should stop at the engine. exa additionally has `_poll_until` (82-100) with no brave counterpart. Overall: high duplication ratio in the shared plumbing; a `_common` module would remove roughly 280+ lines of copy-paste and eliminate the drift risk that a fix in one copy never reaches the other.

findings.description: The entire dual sync/async wrapper set is byte-identical across the two modules: exa/__init__.py lines 133-334 vs brave/__init__.py lines 522-723. This includes _identity_await, _AsyncDict, _AsyncStr, _AsyncList, _AsyncInt, _AsyncFloat, _AsyncBool, _wrap_result, _AsyncScalar, _make_async, _apply_async_to (~200 lines). A `diff` of the two ranges is empty (IDENTICAL). Both also carry the identical module-tail activation call `_apply_async_to(globals())` (exa:5988, brave:7213). Because the copy is verbatim, any bug or fix applied to one copy will silently diverge from the other — the highest-value target for an internal _common module.
findings.evidence: exa 133-137: 'def _identity_await(self): ... if False: # pragma: no cover - makes this a generator (required by await)\n        yield\n    return self' ; exa 140-147 class _AsyncDict(dict) with __await__ returning dict(self) ; exa 216 'def _wrap_result(value):' ; exa 311 'def _apply_async_to(module_dict):' // brave 522-526 identical _identity_await ; brave 529 class _AsyncDict ; brave 605 _wrap_result ; brave 700 _apply_async_to. diff <(sed -n '133,334p' exa/...) <(sed -n '522,723p' brave/...) -> IDENTICAL.
findings.suggestion: Move the whole block into a shared internal module (e.g. search_skills/_common/awaitable.py) and have both exa and brave import it; keep each module's trailing `_apply_async_to(globals())` call pointing at the shared function.

findings.description: The API-key lookup trio is byte-identical: exa/__init__.py lines 411-488 vs brave/__init__.py lines 890-967 (_seek_api_key, _read_key_file, _get_api_key). `diff` of each function range is empty (IDENTICAL). The only differences are the module constants that parameterize it: exa has `_API_KEY_NAMES = ['EXA_API_KEY']`, `_API_LABEL = "exa"` (lines 407-408); brave has `_API_KEY_NAMES = ['BRAVE_API_KEY', 'BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY']`, `_API_LABEL = "brave"` (lines 886-887); both define `_API_KEY_CACHE = {}` (exa:409, brave:888). This is credential-resolution logic duplicated across both, so a behavior change or a path/env bug in one copy will not propagate to the other.
findings.evidence:
Both define verbatim: 'def _seek_api_key(names=None):
    from pathlib import Path
    names = names or _API_KEY_NAMES
    for n in names:
        v = os.environ.get(n, "")
        if v and not v.startswith("${"):
            return v ... stem = names[0].split("_")[0].lower() ... return ""' ; 'def _read_key_file(path, names): ... if k.strip() in names and v.strip(): return v.strip().strip("'"\"")' ; 'def _get_api_key(): label = _API_LABEL ... _API_KEY_CACHE[label] = key; return key'. diff of 411-451/890-930, 453-471/932-950, 473-488/952-967 all -> IDENTICAL.
findings.suggestion: Lift the trio into _common with an injected (key_names, label) or a per-skill config object; each module passes its own _API_KEY_NAMES/_API_LABEL. Preserve the per-label _API_KEY_CACHE dict.

findings.description: The HTTP-engine core is duplicated with only trivial renames: module globals _ENGINE_LIMITS/_CLIENT/_WORKERS plus _http, _pool, _retry_after_seconds, _fanout. exa 26-79 vs brave 23-80. Bodies are verbatim except: `_http` uses `follow_redirects=True` in exa vs `follow_redirects=False` in brave; `_pool` uses `thread_name_prefix="exa"` vs `"brave"`; `_retry_after_seconds` and `_fanout` differ only in docstring text. Note the intended `follow_redirects` difference means a _common _http must be parameterized, not shared as-is. exa additionally defines `_poll_until` (82-100) which has no brave counterpart, so it is exa-specific. These are small, low-risk duplicates.
findings.evidence: _http: exa line 37 'follow_redirects=True' vs brave line 33 'follow_redirects=False' (rest of body identical). _pool: exa 46 'ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=n, thread_name_prefix="exa")' vs brave 42 'thread_name_prefix="brave"'. _retry_after_seconds diff shows only an added docstring line in brave. _fanout diff shows only differing docstrings; the submit/collect loop (pool.submit / fut.result / try-except append) is identical.
findings.suggestion: Move _ENGINE_LIMITS/_CLIENT/_WORKERS/_http/_pool/_retry_after_seconds/_fanout into _common, making _http take a follow_redirects flag and _pool take a thread_name_prefix. Leave exa's _poll_until in exa (no counterpart in brave).

findings.description: Domain/url helpers are CONCEPTUALLY overlapping but DIVERGENT, not near-identical — flagging so a refactor does NOT wrongly merge them. exa `_domain_of` (709-724) computes a registrable domain by stripping scheme/www and slicing the last two labels, and a `hostname` property (693-700) uses urllib.parse.urlparse(...).hostname. brave `_url_host` (114-122) also uses urlparse(...).hostname but lowercases and strips a leading 'www.', and brave `_host` (1081-1084) just reads meta_url.hostname. Same problem space (extract host from a URL), different algorithms and outputs (registrable-domain vs full hostname). The overlap is only the shared `urlparse().hostname` idiom.
findings.evidence: exa 716 'host = url.split("//", 1)[-1].split("/", 1)[0] ... return ".".join(labels[-2:])' (registrable domain) ; exa 698 'urllib.parse.urlparse(u if "://" in u else "https://" + u).hostname' ; brave 119 'host = (urlparse(str(url)).hostname or "").lower()' ; brave 122 'return host[4:] if host.startswith("www.") else host'. No shared function; only the urlparse.hostname idiom matches.
findings.suggestion: Do not fold these into a single shared helper without first unifying the contract (registrable-domain vs host-without-www). If desired, share only a small `urlparse hostname` primitive and keep each module's post-processing separate.

findings.description: deprecations is defined twice (line 5522 and line 5768) inside two pasted copies of the 'Round-18' block (headers at lines 5451 and 5697). LIVE definition is line 5768 (last def wins). The two bodies are NOT identical - they have already drifted: the shadowed copy at 5522 has the extra comment '# the model answer itself flags deprecation - record as a signal.' and names the date variable 'start' ('start = end - timedelta(days=max(1, days))' / 'start_published_date=start.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")'), while the live copy at 5768 omits the comment and renames the variable 'st' ('st = end - timedelta(days=max(1, days))' / 'start_published_date=st.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")'). Behavior is functionally equivalent today, but the divergence proves the two copies are maintained independently: an edit to the shadowed copy at 5522 would be silently inert. deprecations is in __all__ (public API).

...5553:        start = end - timedelta(days=max(1, days))
...5556:                    start_published_date=start.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
5768:def deprecations(query: str, *, days=30, timeout=90.0):
...5798:        st = end - timedelta(days=max(1, days))
...5801:                    start_published_date=st.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),

The first block's unique function api_reference (line 5625) must be preserved.

lenses.summary: Exa (/home/ks/repos/search-skills/exa/src/exa/__init__.py): the 'Round-18' developer-workflows section was pasted into the file TWICE (block headers at lines 5451 and 5697). The second block redefines 5 names from the first block: pkg_releases (5459/5705), _dep_type (5507/5753), deprecations (5522/5768), snippet (5581/5826), code_lint_tips (5672/5870). In all 5 pairs the LAST definition is LIVE (Python last-def-wins); the earlier copies are dead. Four pairs are byte-identical (verified by hashing the full function source) - pure dead code. The deprecations pair has already drifted (comment removed, local variable renamed start->st between the copies), which is the concrete maintenance hazard: a future behavioral edit to the shadowed copy at line 5522 would be silently ignored because the live copy at 5768 shadows it. No crash or wrong-result impact in normal calls today, since every live body matches (functionally) the intended one. The two blocks also each carry a unique function that must be kept (api_reference at 5625 in block 1; is_deprecated at 5894 in block 2). Fix: delete the shadowed block ~5451-5696 while preserving api_reference. Brave (/home/ks/repos/search-skills/brave/src/brave/__init__.py): zero duplicate top-level names - every column-0 def/class name is unique, no findings. No column-0 duplicate variable assignments in either file. No __all__ collisions (the duplicated exa names each appear once in __all__, matching the single live definition).
